summary:
BEYOND TERRA is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform that bridges planetary science and future astronaut exploration.

Powered by authentic NASA and USGS datasets, Beyond Terra transforms complex scientific information into an immersive experience. Users begin with a cinematic 3D Mars globe before exploring an interactive map featuring 46 scientifically significant landmarks, terrain imagery, geological information, and elevation data.

The Marswalk Mission Planner allows users to design expeditions by selecting destinations, creating routes with checkpoints, defining research objectives, assigning equipment, and configuring astronaut crews. Integrated hazard assessments highlight potential terrain challenges using geological and topographic evidence.

The Mars Dashboard provides location-specific insights into elevation, slope, Martian solar time, seasonal conditions, and environmental observations. Its interactive solar visualization demonstrates changing daylight conditions.

By combining scientific discovery, hazard awareness, and mission preparation, Beyond Terra makes planetary data accessible and meaningful.

Our mission is to inspire future explorers to transform scientific curiosity into purposeful Mars exploration plans.
details:
BEYOND TERRA

Project Details

1. Project Overview

BEYOND TERRA is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform developed to bridge the gap between planetary science, accessible scientific education, and the future of human exploration beyond Earth.

Mars has been studied for decades through orbiters, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments. These missions have produced enormous quantities of valuable information about the planet’s surface, geological history, topography, and environmental conditions. However, much of this information is distributed across specialized databases, scientific maps, and technical resources that can be difficult for nonexperts to interpret or use together.

Beyond Terra addresses this challenge by bringing authentic NASA and United States Geological Survey (USGS) datasets into a single, immersive digital environment. Rather than simply displaying Mars as a planet to observe, our platform allows users to explore its surface, investigate scientifically significant locations, interpret terrain information, and develop hypothetical astronaut expeditions.

The project combines a cinematic three-dimensional Mars experience with interactive scientific mapping, geological analysis, a Marswalk Mission Planner, hazard-awareness tools, and a location-specific Mars Dashboard.

Our central idea is simple: What if exploring Mars could move beyond viewing scientific data to actively using that data to plan a mission?

Beyond Terra turns this idea into an interactive prototype, demonstrating how existing planetary datasets can support scientific curiosity, mission preparation, and a deeper understanding of the challenges involved in exploring another world.

2. The Problem We Aim to Solve

Planning exploration on Mars is fundamentally different from planning a journey on Earth.

Mars has unfamiliar terrain, enormous geological formations, impact craters, dunes, steep slopes, and environmental conditions that create challenges for astronauts and robotic explorers. Understanding a potential exploration area requires information from multiple scientific sources.

A researcher might need orbital imagery to understand the landscape, elevation measurements to investigate topography, geological maps to identify formations, and environmental observations to understand local conditions. These datasets are valuable individually, but connecting them into one coherent exploration workflow can be challenging.

This also creates an accessibility problem. Students and aspiring space explorers may be fascinated by Mars yet lack the technical experience required to navigate specialized planetary-science resources.

Beyond Terra was created to address three interconnected needs:

  • Scientific accessibility: Make authentic Martian data easier to explore and understand without requiring advanced planetary-science expertise.
  • Connected mission planning: Allow users to move from discovering a location to designing a scientific expedition within the same interface.
  • Terrain and environmental awareness: Help users recognize that exploration decisions must account for geological evidence, topographic conditions, environmental information, and uncertainty.

Instead of presenting Mars as a collection of disconnected maps and measurements, our project connects scientific information to decisions that a future exploration team might need to consider.

3. How Beyond Terra Works

Beyond Terra follows a connected exploration journey: Discover → Investigate → Plan → Assess → Understand.

A. Cinematic 3D Mars Experience

When users enter Beyond Terra, they are introduced to Mars through an immersive three-dimensional experience.

The opening presents an astronaut-inspired scene, followed by a cinematic transition into a rotating 3D Mars globe. The planet is rendered using Three.js, with carefully coordinated camera movement, lighting, textures, and animation.

Rather than abruptly switching between unrelated pages, the experience transitions from the globe into the interactive Martian map.

This design serves a purpose beyond aesthetics. It establishes the context of exploration and makes the user feel as though they are moving from observing Mars in space to investigating its surface.

The opening is designed to create curiosity and make planetary science approachable, particularly for younger audiences who may be encountering scientific Mars datasets for the first time.

B. Interactive Mars Map and Scientific Landmarks

After the introductory experience, users enter a detailed interactive map of Mars.

The platform uses NASA Mars Trek imagery, allowing users to explore the Martian surface through authentic orbital observations rather than fictional terrain.

The experience includes a curated collection of 46 scientifically significant Martian landmarks, allowing users to discover locations of geological and exploration interest.

Users can search for places, navigate to specific coordinates, zoom into surface formations, and examine information associated with selected locations.

The mapping system also supports a broader search experience using officially named Martian features and rover-related locations.

The platform incorporates imagery from NASA Mars Trek, including global Viking imagery and higher-resolution regional imagery where available, such as Context Camera (CTX) and High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) products.

These sources help users examine the differences between broad planetary geography and localized surface details.

By integrating real observations into an interactive interface, Beyond Terra allows users to investigate Mars as a scientifically documented environment.

C. Terrain, Elevation, and Geological Analysis

One of Beyond Terra’s most important capabilities is its scientific terrain-inspection system.

Users can examine different types of planetary information through selectable map layers, including:

  • Surface imagery.
  • Elevation.
  • Topographic relief.
  • Terrain slope.
  • Geological information.

Elevation and slope information draw on NASA’s Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) data. Geological information incorporates USGS planetary mapping resources.

The platform also includes more detailed terrain information for selected regions, including Jezero Crater, where higher-resolution terrain products are available.

When a user selects a location, the interface can present relevant measurements and geological information, accompanied by explanations of their scientific sources and limitations.

This allows users to investigate questions such as:

What is the elevation of this location? How steep is the surrounding terrain? What geological information is available? How might the terrain affect a hypothetical exploration activity?

An important design decision was to avoid presenting every scientific measurement as equally precise. Different datasets have different resolutions, coverage, and limitations. Beyond Terra therefore distinguishes between available observations, approximate interpretations, and missing information.

This transparency is essential when transforming scientific data into an accessible application.

D. Marswalk Mission Planner

The Marswalk Mission Planner is a central feature of Beyond Terra because it transforms exploration from passive observation into an interactive planning activity.

Users can design hypothetical scientific expeditions by selecting a starting location and destination on the Martian surface.

They can add intermediate checkpoints to represent locations where an exploration team might stop, investigate geological formations, or carry out scientific tasks.

The planner also allows users to define research objectives and organize mission requirements, including equipment and astronaut crew configurations.

Depending on the selected mission configuration, users can examine estimated route characteristics and organize the sequence of their expedition.

For example, a user exploring Jezero Crater could select a starting point, choose a scientifically interesting destination, add checkpoints for geological observations, and assign equipment appropriate to the planned activities.

The resulting mission brings together the geographical route and its scientific purpose.

This feature is designed to encourage users to think beyond the question of where to travel and consider why a location is worth investigating and what an expedition would require.

The Mission Planner is an educational and exploratory prototype. Its routes and resource estimates are not validated astronaut navigation instructions, and they should not be interpreted as operational mission recommendations.

E. Integrated Hazard Assessment

Mars presents a variety of potential terrain hazards, making hazard awareness an important part of exploration planning.

Beyond Terra incorporates a hazard-assessment system that uses available geological and topographic evidence to identify mapped terrain concerns.

These include categories such as steep slopes, dunes, fractures, and depressions where supported by the available datasets.

The hazard system allows users to examine potential challenges associated with a selected location or planned route.

For example, a route that intersects a mapped dune field or an area of significant slope may require additional consideration during hypothetical mission planning.

The purpose of this feature is not to declare whether a route is completely safe or unsafe. Instead, it introduces the concept of evidence-based risk awareness.

This distinction is particularly important because planetary datasets have limited resolution, incomplete coverage, and varying levels of certainty. Small obstacles or local conditions may not be represented in the available maps.

Beyond Terra therefore communicates relevant scientific limitations rather than treating the absence of a mapped hazard as proof of safety.

This approach reflects a key principle behind the project: scientific tools should communicate uncertainty as well as information.

F. Mars Dashboard and Environmental Insights

Beyond Terra’s Mars Dashboard provides another dimension of exploration by helping users understand the environmental context of selected Martian locations.

The dashboard brings together information such as elevation, slope, Martian solar time, seasonal conditions, and available environmental observations.

A particularly engaging feature is the interactive solar visualization, which demonstrates how daylight conditions change over the Martian day.

This introduces users to the relationship between planetary rotation, solar position, local time, and exploration conditions.

The platform also draws on available Mars environmental observations, including information from NASA missions where relevant.

Environmental observations are presented in the context of their source locations and available coverage. They are not represented as real-time weather measurements for every point on Mars.

By integrating environmental information with mapping and mission planning, Beyond Terra encourages users to consider how location, terrain, and time can influence exploration activities.

G. Scientific Sources and Transparency

A defining principle of Beyond Terra is the use of authentic scientific information.

Rather than inventing planetary measurements or using purely decorative terrain data, the platform incorporates publicly available NASA and USGS resources.

Where applicable, users can examine dataset descriptions, measurement details, coverage information, and limitations.

This is especially important when dealing with complex scientific topics. An attractive interface should not come at the expense of scientific accuracy.

Our goal was to make scientific information understandable while preserving the distinction between direct observations, derived measurements, estimates, and unavailable data.

4. Technologies, Tools, and Development Process

Beyond Terra was developed as a browser-based web application using modern frontend technologies, scientific data-processing workflows, and interactive visualization libraries.

Programming Languages and Frameworks

React.js: Used to build the component-based user interface, organize the platform’s features, and manage interactive application states.

TypeScript: Used to implement application logic with stronger type checking, helping maintain consistency across mapping, scientific-data, and mission-planning components.

JavaScript: Used throughout the frontend ecosystem and supporting development scripts.

HTML and CSS: Used to structure and style the application, create responsive layouts, and establish the visual identity of Beyond Terra.

Vite: Used as the frontend development and production-build tool.

Visualization and Mapping

Three.js: Powers the three-dimensional Mars globe, astronaut-inspired introduction, lighting, camera movement, and rendered planetary scenes.

GSAP: Supports cinematic animation sequences and carefully timed transitions between different stages of the experience.

Leaflet: Provides the interactive two-dimensional Martian mapping interface, including map navigation and scientific layer integration.

NASA Mars Trek WMTS: Supplies authentic planetary map imagery used in the interactive exploration environment.

Scientific Data and Processing

The platform incorporates data and mapping products from sources including:

  • NASA Mars Trek planetary imagery.
  • NASA Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) elevation data.
  • NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter imagery and terrain products.
  • USGS geological mapping resources.
  • Publicly available Martian location and planetary feature information.
  • Available rover and environmental observations.

Supporting scripts prepare certain scientific datasets for use in the browser, allowing the application to access and display information through its interactive interface.

Development and Collaboration

The project was developed using a code-based workflow supported by tools such as Visual Studio Code, GitHub, and AI-assisted programming tools, including Claude Code.

GitHub supports source-code management and team collaboration, while the development environment allows different components to be built, integrated, and tested.

The project also uses automated type checking, production builds, and software tests to help identify implementation issues.

Beyond Terra is designed as a web application that can be accessed through a browser without requiring users to install specialized planetary-science software.

No dedicated physical hardware is required to operate the platform.

5. What Makes Beyond Terra Creative and Innovative?

Beyond Terra’s creativity lies not in claiming to have discovered new planetary data, but in reimagining how existing scientific information can be experienced and used.

Many planetary resources are designed primarily for viewing maps, exploring datasets, or studying specific scientific topics.

Beyond Terra connects several activities into one coherent user experience.

From Scientific Observation to Mission Preparation

Instead of ending the experience after a user discovers a location, Beyond Terra allows that discovery to become the starting point for a hypothetical scientific mission.

Users can identify an interesting site, examine the terrain, create a route, organize research objectives, and consider potential hazards.

This creates a meaningful relationship between scientific information and exploration decisions.

An Immersive Introduction to Real Science

The cinematic astronaut opening and three-dimensional Mars globe make the platform engaging without replacing the scientific content.

The immersive presentation draws users into the experience, while the interactive map connects that curiosity to authentic observations.

This combination is intended to make the platform appealing to both students and users interested in space exploration.

Connecting Multiple Scientific Perspectives

A location on Mars cannot be fully understood through imagery alone.

Beyond Terra brings together surface appearance, elevation, geological context, potential terrain hazards, and environmental information.

This encourages users to investigate locations from multiple scientific perspectives rather than relying on a single map or measurement.

Making Scientific Uncertainty Visible

Another important aspect of the project is its treatment of data limitations.

Scientific maps do not provide complete knowledge of every location, and a visually detailed image does not necessarily establish whether terrain is traversable.

Beyond Terra acknowledges these limitations and avoids presenting its prototype calculations as operationally verified decisions.

This makes scientific transparency part of the user experience rather than an afterthought.

6. Factors Our Team Considered

During development, we considered several important scientific, technical, and user-experience factors.

Scientific reliability: We prioritized authentic NASA and USGS information and aimed to distinguish observed data from derived or estimated results.

Dataset coverage and resolution: We considered that scientific datasets vary in geographical coverage and detail. A measurement available for one region may not be available at the same resolution elsewhere.

Usability: We wanted the platform to be approachable for users without specialist knowledge, while retaining enough detail to communicate meaningful scientific information.

Visual design: We balanced cinematic presentation with readable maps, accessible controls, and clear scientific explanations.

Performance: Three-dimensional rendering, map imagery, and scientific layers can be computationally demanding. The application therefore uses browser-based rendering and loading strategies intended to support a responsive experience.

Mission-planning limitations: We recognized that route geometry, terrain measurements, and equipment estimates are not sufficient to certify real astronaut routes. The planner is presented as a demonstration of mission-planning concepts.

Collaboration and integration: We considered how independently developed components could operate within one connected platform without losing their individual functionality.

Future development: We designed the concept around the possibility of incorporating additional scientific datasets, improved route analysis, and more advanced exploration-planning tools over time.

7. Benefits of Beyond Terra

Beyond Terra offers benefits across scientific education, public engagement, and early-stage mission-planning research.

Making Planetary Science Accessible

The platform allows students, educators, and space enthusiasts to interact with scientific Mars information through a visually understandable interface.

Instead of requiring users to navigate multiple technical databases independently, it provides a connected starting point for exploration.

Encouraging Scientific Thinking

Beyond Terra encourages users to ask questions, examine evidence, compare locations, and consider the consequences of exploration decisions.

The Mission Planner also introduces concepts such as research objectives, route selection, resource preparation, and terrain awareness.

Supporting STEM Education

The project can serve as an educational demonstration of how programming, geographical information systems, planetary science, data visualization, and engineering concepts work together.

It also shows how publicly available scientific datasets can be transformed into interactive applications.

Demonstrating the Value of Open Data

NASA and USGS provide scientific resources that can support innovation beyond their original research purposes.

Beyond Terra demonstrates how students and developers can build new experiences using these resources, helping make the benefits of open scientific data more visible.

Building Awareness of Exploration Challenges

By combining terrain information with planning tools, the platform helps users appreciate the complexity of exploring another planet.

It emphasizes that successful exploration requires more than selecting a destination: it involves understanding the environment, defining scientific goals, and considering uncertainty.

8. Intended Impact

Our primary goal is to make Mars exploration more accessible, engaging, and meaningful for the next generation of scientists, engineers, researchers, and explorers.

We believe scientific curiosity becomes more powerful when people can interact with real evidence and use it to investigate their own questions.

Beyond Terra aims to inspire students who may not otherwise have access to specialized planetary-science tools or research environments.

The platform also demonstrates how open scientific information can be transformed into practical educational experiences.

In the longer term, we envision Beyond Terra developing into a more advanced planetary exploration environment that could incorporate additional terrain products, broader environmental datasets, improved route assessment, and more detailed mission simulations.

Potential future extensions include stronger integration between local terrain resolution and route analysis, additional rover observations, and more sophisticated mission resource models.

These are future development possibilities rather than capabilities we claim to have fully implemented today.

The project’s broader impact lies in demonstrating how accessible software can connect planetary observations with the reasoning involved in scientific exploration.

9. Future Vision

Beyond Terra began with a question: How can we make the scientific information already collected about Mars more useful and understandable for future explorers?

Our prototype represents an initial step toward answering that question.

As more scientific data becomes available, we envision expanding the platform’s analytical capabilities, improving the detail of mission simulations, and introducing additional ways for users to compare exploration scenarios.

We also see potential for the platform to support educational activities in which students design hypothetical Mars expeditions, justify their decisions using scientific evidence, and learn how planetary missions balance exploration goals with environmental constraints.

Ultimately, Beyond Terra is not intended to replace professional mission-planning systems. It is intended to demonstrate how authentic planetary information can become the foundation of an accessible, connected, and educational exploration experience.

10. Conclusion

BEYOND TERRA transforms the way users interact with Mars by connecting scientific discovery, terrain analysis, hazard awareness, and mission preparation within a single immersive platform.

Through authentic NASA and USGS datasets, three-dimensional visualization, interactive mapping, and mission-planning tools, the project demonstrates how complex planetary information can become accessible and meaningful.

Our work reflects the belief that the future of space exploration depends not only on collecting more scientific data, but also on finding innovative ways to understand, communicate, and apply the knowledge we already possess.

Beyond Terra is our contribution toward making the Red Planet more accessible and inspiring the next generation to turn scientific curiosity into purposeful exploration.
